whyThisShow: Barton Hall 1980 is the Dead's return to Cornell, and it lives in the long shadow of '77 — one reviewer notes it is "Not as colossal as '77, but then few shows are" [source: 'Not as colossal as '77, but then few shows are']. That said, the second set has a real peak run: a great Space leads into what one listener calls an "incredible, dynamic, loosely/tightened version of Black Peter" [source: 'incredible, dynamic, loosely/tightened version of Black Peter']. The official release on Road Trips Vol. 3 No. 4 pulls from both nights of the May 6–7 run, giving this show partial canonical standing, though Mind Wondrin flags that the Road Trips mastering dragged slowly and has the channels reversed, making it "quite non-essential" [source: 'quite non-essential'] as a source — the miller_26349 SBD is the recommended tape. One reviewer's summary lands the show well: "the curious from '77 Barton come here" and find "a solid show with a great late sequence" [source: 'The curious from '77 Barton come here. What they find is a solid show with a great late sequence'].
listenFor: The Black Peter is the centerpiece: one attendee recalled "jerry standing there in the erie spot light during black peter and the rest of the barn pitch black" [source: 'i can still see jerry standing there in the erie spot light during black peter and the rest of the barn pitch black']. The Space before it is described as "a great, outer-space Space, with a wonderful tranny into a superb Saint" [source: 'a great, outer-space Space, with a wonderful tranny into a superb Saint']. The May '80 Althea gets a quiet nod — one reviewer notes "the May '80 Altheas are always good" while acknowledging this one doesn't reach the Nassau benchmark [source: 'The May '80 Altheas are always good (granted, this one isn't Nassau']. One listener also flagged that Jerry opened the show by attempting Cornell's school song on guitar before the first set began, apparently sight-reading or recalling a folk melody [source: 'Jer gamely attempts Cornell's school song (Far Above Cayuga's Waters). How did he know something so obscure?']. Note that the miller_26349 SBD runs "pitched a hair fast, needing -1% correction" [source: 'needing -1% correction'] if you're particular about pitch.
context: The Dead played Barton Hall three times — 1977, 1980, and 1981 — and this middle visit came almost three years to the day after the famous one. The show falls in the late-70s/early-80s era and was partially released on Road Trips Vol. 3 No. 4 alongside the May 6 show. The best available recording is the SBD gd80-05-07.sbd.miller.26349.sbeok.shnf. Mind Wondrin notes the Road Trips release contains edits in Drums and Space and was mastered at the wrong speed, so the Archive SBD is the preferred listen [source: 'it was mastered at the wrong speed, dragging slowly'].
funFact: By one reviewer's count, this was only the second time the band ever played Shakedown Street directly into Bertha — the first was November 25, 1979 [source: 'this is only the second Shake into Bertha, after 11/25/79'].
headline: Back at Barton Hall, Black Peter in the dark.
